payload.task_text:
Hey, the finance team needs a comprehensive tax compliance audit for our online store. We have a Tax_Regulations.pdf in your workspace along with a guide.md that explains the methodology, so please review those first.

Pull all order data from the store, including each order's total, tax collected, and billing state. Also pull the configured tax rates. Using the methodology in the PDF and guide, compute the expected tax for every order by matching the billing state to the applicable rate. Remember that if no state-specific rate exists, the default rate with an empty state field should be used as a fallback. If a state has multiple rates configured, sum them together.

Create an Excel file called Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Order Tax Audit" with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, and Status. Discrepancy is Actual minus Expected. Status is determined from abs(Discrepancy) using inclusive lower-bound rules: when abs(Discrepancy) <= 0.50 mark Compliant (exactly 0.50 counts as Compliant); when 0.50 < abs(Discrepancy) <= 1.00 classify by sign of Discrepancy (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection, the boundary 1.00 counts here); when abs(Discrepancy) > 1.00 classify by sign in the same direction (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection). The only non-strict boundary is abs == 0.50 which stays Compliant. Include all orders sorted by Order_ID. Round monetary values to 2 decimals, rates to 4 decimals. All values in the workbook must be written as literal numbers (rounded as specified); do not write Excel formulas.

The second sheet should be called "State Summary" with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, and Requires_Filing. Sort by state alphabetically. Compliance_Rate_Pct is the percentage of orders within tolerance rounded to 1 decimal. Requires_Filing is Yes if total actual tax exceeds $100, otherwise No.

The third sheet should be called "Compliance Overview" with two columns Label and Value containing summary metrics: Total_Orders_Audited, Compliant_Orders, Over_Collection_Orders, Under_Collection_Orders, Total_Over_Collected, Total_Under_Collected, Net_Tax_Discrepancy, States_Requiring_Filing, and Overall_Compliance_Rate.

Schedule four quarterly tax filing deadline reminders on the calendar as all-day events. Use the dates from the regulations PDF for the year 2026: April 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2", October 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3", and January 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4".

Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" to collect tax details from our vendors. It should have five questions: vendor name as a short text field (free-form), tax ID number as a short text field (free-form), state of registration as a short text field where respondents enter a US state name or two-letter state code (short_answer type, no hard character limit enforced but expect entries under 40 characters), tax-exempt status as a radio button choice with exactly two options labelled "Yes" and "No", and a text field for uploading or describing their tax certificate (short_answer type allowing a short description or file reference string).

When everything is done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes the complete audit computation into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and calendar/forms writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Tax_Regulations.pdf and guide.md, and freeze the exact state-rate/fallback methodology, the inclusive 0.50/1.00 classifications, the form wording/flags, and the four 2026 filing dates (April 15 "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 "Q2", October 15 "Q3", January 15 "Q4"). Retrieve orders with perPage=100, increasing page to a short or empty page and omitting status; retrieve all tax rates to exhaustion. Preserve order ID, total, total_tax, billing state, and observed status. For each order sum all exact state-specific rates, using the summed empty-state default only if none exists; compute expected tax, actual tax, signed Actual-Expected, and classifications from unrounded values (abs<=0.50 Compliant with 0.50 inclusive; 0.50<abs<=1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection with 1.00 on this boundary; abs>1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection). Read the computation back and freeze one canonical audit_results.json in the workspace containing: all order audit records sorted by Order_ID ascending with 2-decimal monetary values and 4-decimal rates, the alphabetic State Summary rows with Compliance_Rate_Pct (1 decimal) and Requires_Filing (Yes when total actual tax exceeds $100), and the Compliance Overview metrics. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the rates, the PDF, or the guide.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming audit_results.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly three sheets: Order Tax Audit with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, Status and every order sorted by Order_ID; State Summary with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, Requires_Filing sorted alphabetically; Compliance Overview with two columns Label and Value and the nine stated metrics. Write every value as a literal rounded number, never an Excel formula; read all three populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Calendar/forms writer — sole owner of the external outputs. In native parallel, call list_events for each of the four filing dates with ISO midnight timeMin, next-civil-midnight timeMax, sufficient maxResults and orderBy="startTime", and filter exact title/date locally; create only missing reminders with start.dateTime="[filing-date]T00:00:00" and end.dateTime="[next-civil-date]T00:00:00" (all-day, description "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"), omitting timeZone unless the regulations provide one, and retrieve each retained ID with get_event. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Vendor Tax Information, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially in exact task order three add_text_question calls (vendor name, tax ID, state of registration), one add_multiple_choice_question with options ["Yes","No"] for tax-exempt status, and one add_text_question for the certificate description/file-reference field, copying required flags exactly; call get_form and verify title, five-question order, types, options, wording and flags.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass against audit_results.json: workbook cell-for-cell, four exact event identities, and the five-question form structure. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

nodes.text:
You are helping with a tax compliance audit for a WooCommerce store. Your ONLY job is to extract ALL orders from the store into a compact JSON file in the workspace. Do not compute anything, do not create any other files.

Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace

Context you need:
- The store's order list responses get truncated by the tool when they exceed ~50000 characters, so you MUST paginate with perPage=30 (never 100). Each page of 30 orders stays well under the cap and is returned in full.
- Do NOT pass a `status` filter — fetch every order regardless of status.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=30 and page=1, then page=2, page=3, ... incrementing page until the API returns an empty array `[]` (that means you have fetched everything). Keep going until you see an empty page. There are roughly 150 orders, so expect about 5-6 non-empty pages.
2. For every order in every page, extract exactly these fields:
   - id (integer)
   - total (convert the string to float)
   - total_tax (convert the string to float)
   - billing state (the "state" field inside the "billing" object; keep it as-is, may be empty string)
   - status (string, e.g. "completed")
3. Write the result as JSON to: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/orders_compact.json
   Format: {"orders": [{"id": 1, "total": 12.34, "total_tax": 0.62, "state": "CA", "status": "completed"}, ...]} — one object per order, sorted by id ascending.
4. Read the file back and verify: (a) JSON parses, (b) number of orders matches the total you collected, (c) ids are unique and sorted ascending, (d) no order is missing any of the five fields.
5. Print a concise report: total order count, min/max id, the count per status, and the set of distinct billing states (with counts). Also print 3 sample records (first, middle, last by id).

Acceptance criteria: orders_compact.json exists in the workspace, is valid JSON, contains every order exactly once with correct id/total/total_tax/state/status values, sorted by id ascending. Report the summary numbers to me.
Extract all WooCommerce orders compactly

You are the workbook writer for a tax compliance audit. Your ONLY job: create the Excel file Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in the workspace from the canonical frozen payload at:

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/audit_results.json

Do NOT read the store, tax rates, PDF, or guide. Do NOT recompute anything. Copy the numbers from audit_results.json verbatim. Do NOT write any Excel formulas — every cell value must be a literal number (or string where specified).

audit_results.json structure (already computed and frozen by the main agent):
- "orders": list of 150 dicts, already sorted by order_id ascending, each with keys: order_id (int), order_total (float, 2dp), billing_state (str), applicable_rate (float, 4dp), expected_tax (float, 2dp), actual_tax (float, 2dp), discrepancy (float, 2dp), status (str).
- "state_summary": list of 31 dicts, already sorted alphabetically by state, each with keys: state (str), order_count (int), total_revenue (float, 2dp), total_expected_tax (float, 2dp), total_actual_tax (float, 2dp), net_discrepancy (float, 2dp), compliance_rate_pct (float, 1dp), requires_filing (str "Yes"/"No").
- "overview": dict with exactly these keys in this order: Total_Orders_Audited (int), Compliant_Orders (int), Over_Collection_Orders (int), Under_Collection_Orders (int), Total_Over_Collected (float), Total_Under_Collected (float), Net_Tax_Discrepancy (float), States_Requiring_Filing (int), Overall_Compliance_Rate (float, 1dp).

Steps (use the mcp__excel__* tools):
1. Create the workbook: mcp__excel__create_workbook with filepath /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx
2. Ensure exactly three sheets, in this order: "Order Tax Audit", "State Summary", "Compliance Overview". The default sheet created with the workbook will need renaming to "Order Tax Audit" (use mcp__excel__rename_worksheet) or you may create/rename/delete worksheets as needed so that finally there are exactly these three sheets and nothing else (delete any leftover default sheet like "Sheet" or "Sheet1").
3. Sheet "Order Tax Audit": write header row then 150 data rows with mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel, starting at A1. Header row exactly: ["Order_ID","Order_Total","Billing_State","Applicable_Rate","Expected_Tax","Actual_Tax","Discrepancy","Status"]. Data rows follow the payload "orders" list order (already sorted by Order_ID). Write numbers as numbers (int for order_id, float for the monetary/rate values), billing_state and status as strings.
4. Sheet "State Summary": header exactly ["State","Order_Count","Total_Revenue","Total_Expected_Tax","Total_Actual_Tax","Net_Discrepancy","Compliance_Rate_Pct","Requires_Filing"] + 31 data rows in payload "state_summary" order.
5. Sheet "Compliance Overview": two columns, header exactly ["Label","Value"], then 9 rows mapping overview keys in the exact order listed above (Label = key string, Value = number).
6. Verify by reading back every populated range with mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on all three sheets. Confirm: sheet names/order, header rows match exactly, row counts are 151 (header+150), 32 (header+31), 10 (header+9), and every cell equals the corresponding audit_results.json value (compare numbers numerically; strings exactly). Ensure NO cell contains a formula string (nothing starting with "=") and no cell was written as text where a number is expected.
7. Optionally use mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata to confirm the three sheets exist in order.

Return: the absolute path of the file, the sheet order, the row counts for each sheet, and a statement of the cell-for-cell equality check results (all passed / any mismatches listed).
Write Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx

You are the external-workflow operator for a tax compliance audit. Your ONLY job: create four Google Calendar all-day reminders and one Google Form, then verify them. The complete frozen specification is below — do NOT read any store data, PDFs, guides, or any files; do NOT recompute anything.

=== CALENDAR EVENTS (Google Calendar, all-day, year 2026) ===
For each of the four filing deadlines below, the event must exist:
1. 2026-04-15, summary exactly "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1"
2. 2026-07-15, summary exactly "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2"
3. 2026-10-15, summary exactly "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3"
4. 2026-01-15, summary exactly "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4"

Procedure per deadline (these are independent, so run the four list_events calls in parallel):
1. Call mcp__google_calendar__list_events with timeMin="[date]T00:00:00" and timeMax="[next civil day]T00:00:00" (e.g. for 2026-04-15: timeMin="2026-04-15T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-04-16T00:00:00"), maxResults=50, orderBy="startTime". Filter the results locally for an event whose summary matches the exact title above AND whose start date is exactly the target date. If such an event already exists, do NOT create it again — skip to the next one.
2. If missing, create it with mcp__google_calendar__create_event:
   - summary = the exact title
   - start = {"dateTime": "[date]T00:00:00"}  (e.g. "2026-04-15T00:00:00")
   - end   = {"dateTime": "[next civil day]T00:00:00"}  (e.g. "2026-04-16T00:00:00")
   - description = "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"
   - Do NOT pass timeZone (none was specified), no attendees, no location, no recurrence.
3. Immediately after creating, call mcp__google_calendar__get_event with the returned event id and confirm: summary matches, start.dateTime is "[date]T00:00:00", end.dateTime is "[next day]T00:00:00".

=== GOOGLE FORM (title: "Vendor Tax Information") ===
1. Call mcp__google_forms__create_form exactly ONCE with title "Vendor Tax Information". If the call returns anything ambiguous, do NOT retry — report it and continue.
2. Then append questions IN THIS EXACT ORDER (sequential calls, one at a time):
   a. mcp__google_forms__add_text_question: questionTitle "Vendor Name" (free-form short text). Not required.
   b. mcp__google_forms__add_text_question: questionTitle "Tax ID Number" (free-form short text). Not required.
   c. mcp__google_forms__add_text_question: questionTitle "State of Registration" (short text: a US state name or two-letter code; expect <40 characters). Not required.
   d. mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question: questionTitle "Tax-Exempt Status", options exactly ["Yes","No"] (radio button / multiple choice, exactly two options). Not required.
   e. mcp__google_forms__add_text_question: questionTitle "Tax Certificate" (short text: short description or file reference string of the tax certificate). Not required.
   (For all questions, do not mark them required — required flag false.)
3. Verify with mcp__google_forms__get_form: confirm the form title is "Vendor Tax Information" and that there are exactly five questions in the order above with the correct types (a,b,c,e as short-answer text questions; d as a radio/multiple-choice question with options ["Yes","No"]) and the exact wording.

Return: for each of the four events — whether it was created or already existed, its event id, and the get_event confirmation; for the form — the form id, title, and the verified five-question structure (titles, types, options).
Create calendar events and Google Form
